This command can be used to disable, lengthen or shorten, the "sleeping" of the game engine when you are tabbed out, or CS:GO is not your current active window. Usually, when you tab out of CS:GO, the engine will "sleep" for a set amount of milliseconds (repeatedly) to reduce power and resource usage - this will lower your FPS and lag any locally hosted servers when tabbing out. Set this to 0 to completely disable the sleeping of the engine when tabbed out.

arguments.name: Multiplier
arguments.description: The multiplier for friendly damage. If set to 1, damage would be the same to friendly teammates as it would to hostiles. If set to 0, there would be 0 damage done by bullets to friendly teammates. If set to 0.5, bullets would do half damage.

description_valve: How much to reduce damage done to teammates when shot.  Range is from 0 - 1 (with 1 being damage equal to what is done to an enemy)
description_total: This command sets the multiplier for bullet damage made to friendly teammates. The amount of normal damage is multiplied by this number. So if you set this to 0.5 and your bullet would've done 20 damage, it'd be 20 * 0.5, which would mean only 10 damage is done in friendly fire. Setting this to 0 would mean bullets do 0 damage to friendly teammates. Note that this command only has an effect when friendly fire is enabled.

arguments.name: Multiplier
arguments.description: The multiplier for how much damage grenades you throw do to yourself. 1 would mean equal damage, 0 would mean no damage, 0.5 would mean half damage.

description_valve: How much to damage a player does to himself with his own grenade.  Range is from 0 - 1 (with 1 being damage equal to what is done to an enemy)
description_total: This command sets the multiplier for grenade damage from grenades thrown by yourself. Note that this command only has an effect when friendly fire is enabled.

arguments.name: Multiplier
arguments.description: The multiplier for friendly fire damage that isn't done by grenades and bullets. 0 would mean no damage, 1 would mean full damage, 0.6 would mean 60% damage, etc.

description_valve: How much to reduce damage done to teammates by things other than bullets and grenades.  Range is from 0 - 1 (with 1 being damage equal to what is done to an enemy)

arguments.name: FPS Cap

arguments.name: Frames per second
arguments.description: The maximum number of frames per second to be displayed in tools mode when the game window is not in focus. Setting this to 0 removes the limit.

description_valve: Additional frame rate limit while in tools mode and a window other than the game window has focus. Note that fps_max still applies, this only allows the maximum frame rate for tools mode to be lower. 0=no tools specific limit.
description_total: Sets an additional frame rate limit while in tools mode and when a window other than the game window has focus. This allows for lower frame rates in tools mode without affecting the main game's fps_max setting. If set to 0, there is no specific limit for tools mode.

arguments.name: Frame rate limit
arguments.description: Maximum frame rate for the game UI. 0 for no limit.

arguments.description: Set to 0 to disallow players from using healthshots when already at full health. Set to 1 to allow players to use healthshots when already at full health.

description_total: This command, if set to 1 (default) will allow players to use healthshots when already at maximum health. Set to 0 to disallow.

arguments.name: Amount
arguments.description: The amount of health that a healthshot should heal. Default is 50.

description_total: This command sets the amount of health that a healthshot heals.

arguments.name: Multiplier
arguments.description: The multiplier to apply to all damage dealth after consuming a healthshot. 1.5 would multiply damage by 1.5 (a 50% increase).

description_total: This command sets the damage multiplier for damage dealt by a player after having consumed a healthshot. The damage they deal will be multiplied by this number. The amount of time this applies for is set by the healthshot_healthboost_time cvar. Default is 1 (disabled).

arguments.name: Multiplier
arguments.description: The multiplier to apply to a player's movement speed after they consume a health shot. 2.5 would multiply damage by 2.5 (increasing it by 150%).

arguments.name: Seconds
arguments.description: The amount of seconds that a health shot should apply a health (and damage/speed if enabled) boost for.

description_total: This command sets the amount of time, in seconds, that a player receives healthboost for after consuming a healthshot. This is also the amount of time that the damage and speed multipliers will have an effect for.

arguments.name: Framerate

description_total: This command will change the "frame rate" of the host (server). Lower numbers will mean time passes faster, higher numbers will mean time passes slower. Set to 0 to disable.

arguments.description: Ignore user config file setting.

description_total: Controls the behavior of reading or writing to the user config file, specifically whether to ignore the user config file.

arguments.name: Multiplier
arguments.description: The number to multiply the time by. Default is 1, meaning no change. 0.5 would make time go by at half speed, 2 would make things go 2x as fast.

description_valve: Prescale the clock by this amount.
description_total: This can be used to speed up and slow down the speed of time on the server. In otherwords, you can make things go in slow motion or speed the server up with this command.

description_valve: Decrement the timescale by one step
description_total: This command decreases the game's simulation rate by a specific step, making everything in the game move slower.
description_poggu: Decrement the timescale by one step

description_valve: Increment the timescale by one step
description_total: This command increments the game's timescale by one step, effectively speeding up or slowing down the pace of the game. It is flagged as a cheat command, meaning it can usually only be used in non-competitive environments where cheats are enabled.

arguments.name: Impulse #
arguments.description: The number of the impulse you wish to apply. Impulses are:
options: 100 - toggles your flashlight on and off (if you have one)
101 - gives you maximum cash, health and ammo
103 - prints the AI state of the NPC you have under your crosshair. Needs "developer 1" command to work
106 - prints the name, class and model of the entity that is currently under your crosshair to the console
107 - prints the name of the material under your crosshair to the console
108 - sets the NPC under your crosshair as a "debug NPC". We're not too sure what this means, but we think it might make it the target of some debug commands
195 - non-working, should show the shortest path the nearest air node
196 - non-working, should show the shortest path the nearest large node
197 - non-working, should show the shortest path the nearest human node
200 - plays the "holster" animation for the item you current have in your hands. The holster animation is the animation that plays when you switch to an item
201 - creates a player spray under your crosshair
202 - sprays blood on the entity behind your crosshair
202 - players your "player jungle" soundfile. You need to enable cl_customsounds and set cl_soundfile to an eligible WAV file (under 128KB)
203 - does the same as ent_remove, removes the entity that your crosshair is over

description_total: This command is used to influence the spawn intervals of molotv and incendiary grenades for each child.

arguments.description: The maximum depth you want to assign to the child spawn command. Default value for this command is 4.

description_total: This fun console command is used tochange how much damage molotov and incendiary grenades do. When cheats are activated, you can set this value to be incredibly high or incredibly low.

arguments.description: Enter 1 to enable the command and turn on debugging, and a 0 to disable the command and turn it off.

description_total: This command attemps to debug issues that molotov and incendiary grenades may develop. If you notice any issues with them in your game, try using this command.

arguments.name: Spacing
arguments.description: Your desired dlight spacing. The default value for this command is 200, though you can set it to crazy values such as 1 or 10,000.

description_total: This command edits the minimum distance that dlights can be together in the flame animation of molotovs and incendiary grenades. You will see this from a series of connected lasers that appear over the flames when adjusting this command.

arguments.name: Burn Time
arguments.description: How long you want molotov and incendiary grenades to burn for when they explode in seconds. The default value for this command is 7 seconds, but it can be changed to under a second or for minutes at a time.

description_valve: Average lifetime of each flame in seconds
description_total: This console command changes how long the fires burn from molotov and incendiary grenades. It allows you to make them last for just a moment, or for an extended period of time.

arguments.name: Spacing
arguments.description: The distance you want between flame spawns. The default value for this command is 42.

description_valve: Minimum distance between separate flame spawns
description_total: This console command changes the distance between separate flame spawns when using molotov and incendiary grenades.

arguments.name: Reduction Factor
arguments.description: Your desired forward reduction factor for use when the grenades burn. The default value for this command is 0.9.

description_total: This console command changes the forward reduction factor used in molotov and incendiary grenades.

arguments.name: Duration
arguments.description: The time, in seconds, that you want the server to tell that you damaged a teammate with fire. The default value for this command is 6 (seconds).

description_valve: For this long, FF is credited back to the thrower.
description_total: This command sets how long after you've damaged a teammate with a molotov or an incendiary grenade the server tells you that you've damaged someone on your team.

arguments.name: Time
arguments.description: The time it takes for the molotov/incendiary grenade to spread to its entire reach. The default value for this command is 0.02 (seconds).

description_valve: Time between spawning flames for first fire
description_total: This command sets how long it takes for a molotov or incendiary grenade to bloom out and reach its maximum spread. If you set this value higher than the time the molotov is active, it will never reach its full size and stay contained to just a small section of where you threw it.

arguments.name: Time
arguments.description: The max time it will take for a grenade's child flames to spawn in second. The higher you set this, the longer it takes. Default value for this command is 0.5.

description_valve: Largest time interval for child flame spawning
description_total: Use this command to set the longest period of time that can pass before a molotov or incendiary grenade's child flames spawn.

arguments.name: Max Flames
arguments.description: The max amount of flames you want to be able to spawn. Sadly, setting it to a number like 1,000 won't produce 1,000 flames when using a molotov or incendiary grenade.

description_valve: Maximum number of flames that can be created
description_total: This command is used to set the maximum number of flames that can be created from a single molotov or an incendiary grenade.

arguments.name: Range
arguments.description: The maximum range that flames can spread from where you threw the grenade. The default value for this command is 150.

description_valve: Maximum distance flames can spread from their initial ignition point
description_total: This command sets the maximum distance that flames from a molotov or incendiary grenade can spread from their initial point of impact with the ground.

arguments.name: Time
arguments.description: The time until new flames will try and spawn more new flames. The default value for this command is 3 seconds.

description_valve: Duration each new flame will attempt to spawn new flames
description_total: This command is the time in seconds that each new flame in an incendiary grenade or molotov will try to create new flames.

arguments.description: Enter a 0 after this command topreventfire grenades from leaving scorch decals, and a 1 after the command to leave them on (default).

description_total: You can use this console command to prevent molotovs and incendiary grenades you throw from leaving scorch decals (scorch marks) on the ground once they burn out.

arguments.name: Density
arguments.description: The thickness of the smoke.

description_total: Adjusts the density of smoke produced by incendiary grenades or Molotov cocktails. A higher number makes smoke thicker.

arguments.name: Degrees
arguments.description: The angle in degrees that the child flames burn based off their parents position. The default value for this command is 45 degrees.

description_valve: Angular change from parent
description_total: This console command adjusts the angle from which child flames burn to their parent. You can use it to edit slightly the way that molotovs spread when they burn.

arguments.name: Offset
arguments.description: The desired offset you want your fire grenades to burn at. The default value for this command is 20.

description_total: This command edits the surface offset used in incendiary grenades and molotovs when they hit the ground and begin burning.

arguments.name: Velocity
arguments.description: The desired velocity of the flame's decay. The default value for this command is 0.2.

description_total: This console command is used to edit the velocity of the decay factor in the flames of molotov and incendiary grenades.

arguments.name: Velocity
arguments.description: The desired velocity of the grenade. The default value for this command is 0.003.

arguments.description: Enter 0 to make it so that players cannot vote for the next map (random). Enter 1 (default) to allow players to vote for the next map.

description_valve: Whether or not players vote for the next map at the end of the match when the final scoreboard comes up
description_total: This command enables and disables the option for players to vote for the next map at the end of the game. Default is 1 (which allows players to vote).

arguments.description: Enter 0 to disallow players for voting for the map that was just played. Enter 1 (default) to allow players to vote for the same map again.

description_valve: If set, keeps the current map in the list of voting options.  If not set, the current map will not appear in the list of voting options.
description_total: This command sets whether or not the current map is allowed to be voted for at the end of the game. Default is enabled, meaning players can vote again for the same map.

description_valve: Modes available for endmatch voting during War Games. Separate names with spaces.
description_total: This command shows you what modes you can vote for when a match ends during War Games.

arguments.name: Maps
arguments.description: The amount of maps that can be shown in the vote. By default this command is set to 3.

description_valve: Maximum number of maps to include in endmatch voting during War Games
description_total: This command changes the maximum number of maps that can be shown in the end game vote when in War Games.

arguments.name: Modes
arguments.description: The max number of modes that can be voted on. The default value for this command is 1.

description_valve: Maximum number of other War Games to include in endmatch voting during War Games
description_total: This command sets the maximum amount of other War Games modes to be included in the end of map vote.

arguments.name: Amount
arguments.description: The amount of players required to join the server for warmup to end and the game to start (instantly). Set to 0 to wait until all players connect.

description_valve: Number of players required to be connected to end warmup early. 0 to require maximum players for mode.
description_total: This command sets the amount of players that need to connect to the game for warmup to be ended early. Set to 0 to wait until all players are connected (default).

arguments.name: X
arguments.description: Every X rounds, reset every player on the server's equipment. If you enter a 7, every 7th round everyone will have their equipment reset. Use a 0 to never reset people's equipment.

description_valve: Reset all player equipment every N rounds (0 for never)
description_total: This cheat command lets you reset every player's equipment every X amount of rounds.

arguments.description: Determines whether fists replace the melee weapon when dropped.

description_total: This command determines if players will default to using fists when their melee weapon is dropped, and conversely, lose the ability to use fists when a melee weapon is picked up.

arguments.description: Enter a 1 after the command to turn it on (default), and a 0 to turn it off.

description_valve: Makes the server always play footstep sounds. Clients never calculate footstep sounds locally, instead relying on the server.
description_total: This command decides whether or not the server always plays footstep sounds. This is used to produce footsteps in your client.

arguments.name: Seconds
arguments.description: The time, in seconds, that a player has to choose a team before they are automatically given a team.

description_valve: The amount of time a player has on the team screen to make a selection before being auto-teamed
description_total: This command sets the duration, in seconds, that the game will allow for a player to choose a team. After this time period, a team is automatically chosen for them. Default duration is 15 seconds.

arguments.description: Set this to 0 to allow players to spectate any team. Set this to 1 to allow players to only spectate their own team. Set this to 2 to disallow spectating, players will be shown a black screen until the next round.

description_valve: Restricts spectator modes for dead players
description_total: This command sets the scope spectators have (i.e. who players can spectate when they die). See argument information for scopes.

arguments.name: Limit
arguments.description: The maximum number of kills before the map ends. Set to 0 to disable.

description_total: Sets the maximum number of kills a player or team can achieve before the current map ends. A value of 0 disables this limit.

arguments.description: Enter a 0 here to disable free armor and helmet at the start of the round  / on respawn (default). Enter 1 to give a free vest to all players on respawn. Enter 2 to give a free vest and helmet to all players on respawn.

description_valve: Determines whether kevlar (1+) and/or helmet (2+) are given automatically.
description_total: This command, if set to 1, will make each player spawn with a vest and if set to 2, will make players respawn with both a vest and a helmet. Default is 0 (no vest or helmet).

arguments.name: Seconds
arguments.description: The amount of time, in seconds, that players should be frozen for at the start of the round.

description_valve: how many seconds to keep players frozen when the round starts
description_total: This command sets how long players are frozen for at the start of each the round. This freeze time allows players to buy their gear and discuss tactics before the round begins. Default is 15 seconds.

arguments.description: Enter a 0 here to disable friendly fire, meaning teammates won't be able to hurt eachother. Enter a 1 here to enable friendly fire.

description_valve: Allows team members to injure other members of their team
description_total: This command can be used to enable and disable friendly fire. When friendly fire is enabled, players can damage their own teammates. The default setting for this command depends on gamemode. Competitive game modes have friendly fire enabled, casual do not.

arguments.description: Enter 0 to make the C4 not be spawned. Enter 1 to make the C4 be given to a random T at the start of the round.

description_valve: Whether this map should spawn a c4 bomb for a player or not.
description_total: This command sets whether or not a player (on T side) should be given a bomb at the start of the round. Default depends on gamemode, for demolition gamemodes, this setting is enabled (1).

arguments.name: DPS
arguments.description: The damage per second you want to do to players. The default value for this command is 0 (off).

description_valve: If above 0, deal non-lethal damage to players over time.
description_total: Entering a value after this command causes each player in the server to take that amount of damage per second. This is non-lethal, so they can't die from this.

arguments.name: Interval
arguments.description: The interval of waves after which bot difficulty is adjusted.

description_total: Adjusts the difficulty of guardian bots every nth wave specifically when utilizing behavior trees.

arguments.name: Round Number
arguments.description: The round from which the difficulty cap will start applying.

description_total: Applies a difficulty cap to the bots starting from the specified round in Guardian game mode. This cap influences how challenging the AI bots will be.

arguments.name: Difficulty level
arguments.description: The initial difficulty level for bots in Guardian mode.

description_total: Sets the starting difficulty level for Guardian mode bots.

arguments.name: Number of Bots
arguments.description: The number of bots to increase difficulty per wave.

description_total: Controls the number of bots whose difficulty level increases per wave in Guardian mode, making them harder to defeat.

arguments.name: X Coordinate
arguments.description: The X coordinate for the custom bomb plant X mark location.

arguments.name: Y Coordinate
arguments.description: The Y coordinate for the custom bomb plant X mark location.

arguments.name: Z Coordinate
arguments.description: The Z coordinate for the custom bomb plant X mark location.

description_valve: x,y,z to display an X for the bomb plant in guardian missions with custom bomb plant boundaries.
description_total: Specifies the x, y, z coordinates to display an X marker for the bomb plant area in Guardian missions with custom bomb plant boundaries.

arguments.name: Money
arguments.description: The money bots get when a player clears a wave. This is not additive, so they will have this command at the start of each new wave.

description_total: This console command controls how much money bots get each wave that a player completes.

arguments.name: Time in seconds
arguments.description: The amount of time in seconds after which bots will be forced to collect hostages if no enemy has been seen.

description_total: This command sets the amount of time (in seconds) after which bots are forced to collect hostages if they haven't seen any enemy.

arguments.description: Determines if guardian bots receive grenades at the start of each wave.

description_total: This command determines whether guardian bots receive grenades at the start of each wave in the Guardian game mode.

arguments.name: Localization String Token
arguments.description: The localization string token to be used on the HUD.

description_total: Specifies the localization string token to use on the HUD for a Guardian mission; it defaults to indicating kills with a specific weapon.
N/A

arguments.name: Distance
arguments.description: Distance from a bombsite before a player is killed. The default value for this command is 2000.

description_total: This console command sets how far a player can get from the bombsite before they are killed.

arguments.name: Distance
arguments.description: Distance from a bombsite before players are warned that they're going too far. The default value for this command is 1300.

description_total: This console command sets how far a player can get from the bombsite before they are warned that they are moving too far away from the bombsite.

arguments.name: Kills
arguments.description: The kills needed with a special weapon. The default value for this command is 10.

description_total: In an operation, this is the number of kills you need to get with a special weapon.

arguments.name: Weapon
arguments.description: The weapon code of the special weapon you want to use. The default value for this command is awp for the AWP.

description_total: This is the special weapon needed to finish a mission in an operation to achieve the special kill count.

description_valve: If set to the index of a bombsite, will cause random spawns to be only created near that site.
description_total: N/A

arguments.description: Enter 0 to disable team switching at half time. Enter 1 to enable team switching at half time (default).

description_valve: Determines whether the match switches sides in a halftime event.
description_total: This command sets whether or not teams are switched at half time. Default is 1, which is enabled.

arguments.name: Seconds
arguments.description: The duration of half time, in seconds. Default is 15.

description_valve: Target number of seconds that halftime lasts; shortened if team intros are active
description_total: This command sets the duration of half time, in seconds.

arguments.description: Enter a 1 after the command to attempt to pause the game during halftime, and a 0 after the command to not do so (default).

description_valve: Set to 1 to pause match after halftime countdown elapses. Match must be resumed by vote or admin.
description_total: This command, when approved by the server admin, pauses the game when halftime has been reached (just as the 15th round is won total, combining the team's scores).

arguments.description: Enter 0 to make it so that the match is not paused at half time - after the halftime countdown, gameplay will be resumed. Enter 1 to pause the match at half time until resumed.

description_valve: Set to 1 to stay in halftime indefinitely. Set to 0 to resume the timer.
description_total: This command can make it so that the match is paused at half time, and will not resume until unpaused manually. By default this is disabled (0).

arguments.name: Aimpunch
arguments.description: A number used to signify the extra aimpunch the player wearing the assault suit receives when getting shot. The default value for this is 1.

description_total: This console command determines how muchextraaim punch a player receives when getting shot wearing an assault suit.

arguments.name: Time
arguments.description: The cooldown time in minutes before a player is allowed to purchase the assault suit again. The default value for this command is 5.

description_total: Sets the cooldown time on purchasing an assault suit in select game modes.

arguments.description: Enter a 0.5 after this command to set the draw speed to half speed, and a 1 after the command to set draw speed to normal. The default value for the command is 0.8.

description_total: This command sets how quick a player wearing the heavy assault suit (available in Heavy Assault Suit mode) can draw their weapon.

arguments.name: Speed
arguments.description: The maximum movement speed of a player when they are in the heavy assault suit. The default value for this command is 130.

description_total: This command determines the max movement speed of a player when they are in the heavy assault suit.

arguments.description: Enter a 0.5 after the command to half the damage players take from bullets when in a heavy assault suit. Enter a 1 after the command to not change how much bullet damage they receive. Default value for this command is 1.

description_total: This command can be used to make players in heavy assault suits take less damage than usual from bullets.

arguments.name: Amount
arguments.description: The maximum amount of hostages that should be spawned at the start of the round. Default is 2.

description_valve: Maximum number of hostages to spawn.
description_total: This command sets the maximum amount of hostages that should be spawned at the start of the round.

arguments.description: Enter 0 to make it so the extra time is not added when a hostage is rescued. Enter 1 to enable extra time when a hostage is rescued (default).

description_valve: Additional time added to round time if a hostage is reached by a CT.
description_total: This command sets whether or not extra time should be added to the round if/when a hostage is rescued. Default is 1 (enabled).

arguments.name: Multiplier
arguments.description: The number to multiply run speed by when you are carrying a hostage.

description_valve: Default is 1.0, slow down hostages by setting this to < 1.0.
description_total: This command sets how run speed is affected when you are carrying a hostage. 0.5 = half speed, 1.5 = 150% speed.

arguments.description: Enter 0 here to make it so that hostages spawn at a randomly selected location (out of the pre-defined locations) (default). Enter 1 here to make hostages spawn at the furthest possible location.

description_valve: When enabled will consistently force the farthest hostages to spawn.
description_total: This setting, if enabled, makes hostages spawn at the furthest possible location. By default this is set to 0 (disabled).

arguments.name: Positions
arguments.description: Enter each spawn position you wish to force each round, each position should be separated by a comma. To force position 2 and 3, you'd enter "2,3" (quotes not needed).

description_valve: Comma separated list of zero based indices to force spawn positions, e.g. '0,2' or '1,6'
description_total: This command can be used to force spawn positions. Enter each spawn position you wish to be the same every round (the number of the spawn position), with each spawn potion separated by a comma.

arguments.name: X1,Y1,Z1,X2,Y2,Z2,...
arguments.description: Comma separated list of XYZ coordinates for hostage spawn points.

description_valve: Comma separated list of xyz locations to force spawn positions, e.g. 'x1 y1 z1,x2 y2 z2'
description_total: Sets specific XYZ coordinates to force the spawn positions of hostages in the game. Useful for creating custom hostage scenarios or for testing.

arguments.description: Enter 0 to make hostages spawn at random locations at the start of each round. Enter 1 to make it so that hostages spawn in the same locations as round 1 every round (the first round will still be randomized, but subsequent rounds will be the same positions.)

description_valve: 0 = spawn hostages randomly every round, 1 = same spawns for entire match.
description_total: This command will set whether or not the location of hostages is randomized each round, or the same throughout the game. Default is 1 (same for entire match).

arguments.description: Set this to 0 to make it so that hostages cannot take damage (default). Set this to 1 to allow hostages to take damage.

description_valve: Whether or not hostages can be hurt.
description_total: This command sets whether or not hostages can take damage. Default is 0 (unable to take damage).

arguments.name: Any / CT / T
arguments.description: Enter "any" to allow players to join any team. Enter "t" to allow non-bot players only on terrorist team. Enter "ct" to allow non-bot players only on counter-terrorist team.

description_valve: Restricts human players to a single team {any, CT, T}
description_total: This command can be used to restrict non-bot players to a specified team. Default is any team. See argument information for options.

arguments.description: This command, if enabled, would make the game ignore the conditions that usually end the round (e.g. everyone on a team dying, bomb exploding). When enabled, the round will last forever, or until you manually end it or disable this setting. Default is 0 (do not ignore win conditions).

description_valve: Ignore conditions which would end the current round
description_total: This command can be used to enable and disable round win conditions. If round win conditions are disabled (ignored), then the conditions that would usually make a round end (e.g. bomb exploding, team being eliminated) will no longer make the round end - the round would last forever, until manually ended. By default, this command is disabled (meaning win conditions are not ignored).

arguments.name: Items
arguments.description: A list of comma-separated items you wish to ban from your server. By default there are no banned items.

description_valve: Set this convar to a comma-delimited list of definition indices of weapons that should be prohibited from use.
description_total: This command allows you to prohibit items or guns from being used in your server.

arguments.name: Seconds
arguments.description: The amount of time, in seconds, that a player can join a team for after the round has started. Default is 0 (players cannot join after round has started).

description_valve: Number of seconds after round start to allow a player to join a game
description_total: This command sets the amount of time (in seconds) that a player can join the game for after a round starts. If they join after this period, they will be added to the spectators until the next round.

arguments.name: Amount
arguments.description: The maximum difference in players each team can have. A player cannot join a team, if them joining would make the difference in players between this team and the other team larger than this number. Set to 0 to disable team limiting.

description_valve: Max # of players 1 team can have over another (0 disables check)
description_total: This command sets the maximum amount of different in players that there can be between two teams. If this was set to 1, if the CT team had 3 and T team had 2, a new player would not be able to join the CT team. Setting this to 0 disables the check. Default is 2.

arguments.description: Set to 0 (default) to turn attack logging off. Set to 1 to only log enemy combat damage. Set to 2 to only log friendly combat damage. Set to 3 to log all forms of combat damage (both friendly and enemy).

description_valve: Logs attacks.  Values are: 0=off, 1=enemy, 2=teammate, 3=both)
description_total: This command sets the server "combat" logging setting. See argument information for help.

arguments.description: Enter a 1 after this command to turn it on and start producing log entries, and a 0 after the command to turn it off (default).

description_valve: Logs a line any time a player acquires or loses an item.
description_total: Turning this command on produces a log any time that a player acquires a new weapon.
N/A
N/A
N/A

arguments.description: Enter a 1 after the command to enable money logging so you can track what you spend and earn, and a 0 after the command to turn it off (default).

description_valve: Enables money logging.  Values are: 0=off, 1=on
description_total: This command is ued to turn money logging on or off.

arguments.description: Set this to 0 to make it so that the game will be played out, regardless of whether or not it is impossible for one of the teams to catch up with the score and win. Set this to 1 (default) to end the match when one team reaches a score that would make it impossible for the other team to catch up.

description_valve: Can a team clinch and end the match by being so far ahead that the other team has no way to catching up?
description_total: This command sets whether or not the game should be automatically ended when it is not possible for another team to catch up. For example, in competitive, when a team gets 16 rounds, it would be impossible for the other team to catch up (so the match would be ended). If this setting was set to 0 (disabled), the game would not be ended when 16 rounds were reached. By default is this 1 (enabled).

arguments.description: Set this to 0 to not change the level at the end of the game if the map is the same (default). Set this to 1 to reload the game's map if it is the same.

description_valve: At the end of the match, perform a changelevel even if next map is the same
description_total: This command sets whether or not the map should perform a changelevel when the next map is the same map. Default is off (0), meaning scores/etc will be reset at the end of a match, and the map will not be loaded again if it is the same.

arguments.description: Set this to 0 to not restart the current map, and instead load the next map at the end of the game. Set this to 1 to restart the match (as opposed to loading the next map) at the end of the match in play.

description_valve: At the end of the match, perform a restart instead of loading a new map
description_total: This command sets whether or not, at the end of the game, the current game (and map) is simply restarted or if a new map is loaded.

arguments.name: Seconds
arguments.description: The amount of time, in seconds, that the game should countdown for, before restarting the match (at the end of a match).

description_valve: Time (in seconds) until a match restarts.
description_total: This command sets how long it takes, in seconds, for a match to restart. This countdown is used at the end of a match, not when the mp_restartgame command is used.

arguments.description: Enter a 0 after the command to not allow players to buy any armor. Enter a 1 to allow players to buy just a Kevlar body. Enter a 2 to allow players to purchase a Kevlar body and helmet.

description_valve: Determines the highest level of armor allowed to be purchased. (0) None, (1) Kevlar, (2) Helmet
description_total: This command sets what level of armor can be purchased in your server - no armor, kevlar body, or kevlar body and helmet.

arguments.name: Amount
arguments.description: The maximum amount of money that a player can have at any given time. A player's balance will not go above this amount, it will be capped at this value.

description_valve: maximum amount of money allowed in a player's account
description_total: This command sets the maximum amount of money that any player can have at a given time. Maximum possible value is 65,535 due to technical limitations.

arguments.name: Amount
arguments.description: The maximum amount of rounds that the server will play before restarting.

description_valve: max number of rounds to play before server changes maps
description_total: This command sets the maximum amount of rounds that the server will play for.

arguments.name: Minimum Halftime Duration
arguments.description: The minimum number of seconds halftime will last.

description_valve: Minimum number of seconds that halftime lasts even if team intros are active
description_total: Defines the minimum duration of halftime in seconds. This duration applies even if team introductions are active.

arguments.name: Team
arguments.description: Specifies which team's timeout settings are being modified (either CT for Counter-Terrorists or T for Terrorists).

arguments.name: Number of Timeouts
arguments.description: The number of timeouts to allow. Use a specific number to set a limit, or -1 for unlimited timeouts.

description_valve: T> <N>, e.g., mp_modify ct -1
description_total: This command is used to modify the timeout durations for either the Counter-Terrorist (CT) or Terrorist (T) teams. It adjusts the number of timeouts allowed for a team or the duration.
description_poggu: mp_modify_timeouts <CT|T> <N>, e.g., mp_modify ct -1

arguments.description: Set to 0 to allow all players to rescue hostages. Set to 1 to make it so that only counter-terrorists can rescue hostages (default).

description_total: This command, if set to 1 (default on all game modes with the exception of Danger Zone), will make it so that only counter-terrorist players can rescue hostages. Set to 0 to allow all players to rescue hostages.

arguments.description: Enter 0 here to disable overtime (default). Enter 1 here to enable overtime.

description_valve: If a match ends in a tie, use overtime rules to determine winner
description_total: This command can be used to enable or disable overtime. Overtime is when extra rounds are played out to decide a winner, if the match ends with a tie. By default this is disabled (0). Set the amount of overtime rounds with mp_overtime_maxrounds.

arguments.description: Enter 0 here to disable a pause in between each overtime half (default). Enter 1 here to enable a pause (that has to be manually unpaused) at the end of each overtime half.

description_valve: If set to 1 will set mp_halftime_pausetimer to 1 before every half of overtime. Set mp_halftime_pausetimer to 0 to resume the timer.
description_total: This command can be used to enable or disable the pausing of the match in between each overtime half. If set to 1 (enabled), the match will pause after each overtime half and require a manual unpause before it is resumed. Default is 0 (off).

arguments.name: Overtime Limit
arguments.description: The maximum number of overtimes allowed in a match.

description_valve: When overtime is enabled, only so many overtimes can be played
description_total: Specifies the maximum number of overtimes allowed in a match when the overtime feature is enabled. A value of 0 implies that there is no limit to the number of overtimes.

arguments.name: Amount
arguments.description: The maximum amount of rounds for each overtime session. The amount required to win will be automatically adjusted.

description_valve: When overtime is enabled play additional rounds to determine winner
description_total: This command sets the maximum amount of rounds for each overtime session. Half time will be made at half of this value (i.e. at 6 max rounds, half time will be after 3 rounds).

arguments.name: Amount
arguments.description: The amount of money that each player should have at the start of an overtime half.

description_valve: Money assigned to all players at start of every overtime half
description_total: This command sets the amount of cash that players start with at the beginning of each overtime half. Default is 10,000.

description_valve: Pause the match in the next freeze time
description_total: This command will pause the match at the end of the current round. Resume with mp_unpause_match.
description_poggu: Pause the match in the next freeze time

arguments.description: Set to 0 to only allow the C4 to be planted at bombsites (default). Set to 1 to allow the C4 to be planted at any location.

description_total: This command, if set to 1, allows players to plant C4s at any location. If set to 0, the C4 can only be planted at bomb sites.

arguments.description: Set this to 0 to disable. Set this to 1 to enable.

description_valve: Players can earn money by performing in-game actions
description_total: This command sets whether or not players should be able to earn money for performing in-game actions.

arguments.description: Set this to 0 to show all names, set this to 1 to show only your team's names, set this to 2 to show no names.

description_valve: Controls what information player see in the status bar: 0 all names; 1 team names; 2 no names
description_total: This command sets what players can see in the status bar. See argument information for help.

description_valve: Number of seconds to delay showing information in the status bar
description_total: This command sets the amount of time, in seconds, that the game should wait before showing information in the status bar. Default is 0.

arguments.name: Seconds
arguments.description: The amount of time, in seconds, that the status bar should wait before updating with new information.

description_valve: Number of seconds to keep showing old information in the status bar
description_total: This command sets the amount of seconds the status bar should hold old information for before updating with new information. Default is 0 (always updating).

arguments.description: Enable or disable the purchasing of the promoted item.

description_valve: Allow the purchasing of the promoted item.
description_total: This command is used to control whether players can purchase the promoted item in the game. When enabled, players will have the option to buy a specific item that is being promoted, typically for a limited time.

arguments.description: Options are:
options: 1 - everyone spawns in random locations (like deathmatch)
2 - only terrorists spawn at random locations, CTs spawn at their spawn
3 - only CTs spawn at random locations, terrorists spawn at their spawn

description_valve: Determines whether players are to spawn. 0 = default; 1 = both teams; 2 = Terrorists; 3 = CTs.
description_total: This command sets whether or not players should spawn randomly (e.g. in deathmatch). If not enabled (default for non-deathmatch gamemodes), players will spawn at the map's spawn locations (T or CT spawn, relative to team). See argument information for help.

arguments.description: Enter a 1 after the command to turn on distance testing, and a 0 after the command to turn it off.

description_valve: If using mp_randomspawn, determines whether to test distance when selecting this spot.
description_total: If you are using the mp_randomspawn command, this command is used to determine whether or not you test distance with that setting.

arguments.description: Set this to 0 to disable line of sight check. Set this to 1 to try to spawn players in locations that aren't currently in the view of any players.

description_valve: If using mp_randomspawn, determines whether to test Line of Sight when spawning.
description_total: This command, if enabled, will make the server try to spawn players outside of the line of sight of another player (i.e. spawn players in locations that other players aren't looking at).

arguments.description: Set to 0 to make it so that guns are picked up when walked over (default). Set to 1 to require players to press E (or +use) on weapons in order to pick them up.

description_valve: Whether guns must be +used to acquire or default is touch-to-pickup
description_total: This command, if set to 1, will make it so that guns must be +used on (usually the E key) in order to be picked up by players. Default is 0 (guns are picked up when they are walked over).

arguments.name: Seconds
arguments.description: The amount of time, in seconds, that players should be immune for after spawning in the map.

description_valve: How many seconds after respawn immunity lasts. Set to negative value to disable warmup immunity.
description_total: This command sets how many seconds players will be immune for after they respawn, used for deathmatch gamemodes. Default is 0 in non-deathmatch gamemodes.

arguments.description: Set to 0 to make it so that CTs only respawn at the start of the next round. Set to 1 to make CTs respawn after death.

description_valve: When set to 1, counter-terrorists will respawn after dying.
description_total: This command will set whether or not counter-terrorists will respawn after dying.

arguments.description: Set to 0 to make it so that terrorists only respawn at the start of the next round. Set to 1 to make terrorists respawn after death.

description_valve: When set to 1, terrorists will respawn after dying.
description_total: This command will set whether or not terrorists will respawn after dying.

arguments.name: Seconds

description_valve: Force the view model to draw, even when in 3rd person
description_total: This command forces the view model (the visual representation of the player's weapon and arms) to always be visible, even when the camera is in third-person view. This can be useful for content creators or those wanting a consistent visual reference.

arguments.name: FOV
arguments.description: A number - your desired field of view. By default this is 60. You can set this to a maximum of 68.

description_valve: Viewmodel FOV
description_total: This command sets your client's FOV to the specified number. You can set your FOV to a maximum of 68 using this command. The default field of view is 60.

arguments.description: Determines whether the viewmodel offset randomization is enabled or not.

description_valve: randomly change viewmodel offsets to visualize range
description_total: This command randomly changes the viewmodel offsets within a certain range to help visualize the extent of possible viewmodel positions.

arguments.name: X Offset
arguments.description: Set this to a number between 2.5 and -2.5. -2.5 would be closest to the middle of the screen. 2.5 would be closest to the edge of the screen.

description_valve: viewmodel_offset_x
description_total: This command sets the X offset of your view model - i.e. how far left or right it is. Your view model is your hand (and the gun in it) that displays in first person mode. The maximum value is 2.5 and the minimum value is -2.5.

arguments.name: Y Offset
arguments.description: Set this to a number between 2 and -2. 2 would be closest to the top of the screen. -2 would be closest to the bottom of the screen.

description_valve: viewmodel_offset_y
description_total: This command sets the Y offset of your view model - i.e. how close or far from your character is. Your view model is your hand (and the gun in it) that displays in first person mode. The maximum value is 2 and the minimum value is -2.

arguments.name: Z Offset
arguments.description: Set this to a number between 2 and -2. 2 would put your viewmodel as far in front of you as possible. -2 put your viewmodel as close as possible to you.

description_valve: viewmodel_offset_z
description_total: This command sets the Z offset of your view model - i.e. how far up or down it is. Your view model is your hand (and the gun in it) that displays in first person mode. The maximum value is 2 and the minimum value is -2.

arguments.description: A number to represent your desired preset. Options are:

description_valve: 1:'Desktop', 2:'Couch', 3:'Classic'
description_total: This command will set your X/Y/Z viewmodel offsets to a preset configuration. See argument information for help.
